title: Bright Dawn project map

last_change.what: With the graphics hardware, outlines and the smoothing of polygon edges (anti-aliasing) are drawn by the processor's rules, at any resolution: the polygons are drawn once more as the DS draws them, on the graphics hardware.

lines.text: Works: memory map, registers, interrupts, timers, DMA, math unit, cartridge, 2D engines, 3D geometry and renderer, display capture, buttons, touch.
Partly: second processor stand-in (4 of its services, the save chip kept in a file; no music sequences),
time (one cycle per instruction). The game runs to its name entry, built or interpreted.
Vulkan; 3D on the GPU up to 8x
sound is made, not played yet
window, paths, settings, frame clock, crash and hang notes

parts.now: Checks the ROM, reads its file system, archives and every kind of compression the game uses.
Decodes the menus' pictures and the game's font (NFTR) for the launcher. Textures, models and sounds: not yet.
Planned: replace game files without changing the ROM.

Translates 17,076 functions of the game's code, and the interrupt entry of Bright Dawn's own BIOS, to C++, on your computer, with interrupt polls and instruction counts. Where code puts its own return address in lr before a jump, that address is translated too, and so is the place a saved thread context is resumed at.
Downloads its compiler (and Python on Windows) for the build and deletes it after. The downloaded compiler is not yet tried on a real build.
Builds, loads and runs: reaches the name entry like the interpreted game, about twice as fast (600 frames in 11 s instead of 24).

Runs translated code with the interpreter behind it. Interrupts are taken where translated code polls for them. Calls that never return no longer pile up until the program crashes (the Windows crash after about 7 minutes). Each run writes a log of the places run in the interpreter, with why.

The console model runs the game from the title screen to battles, with a save from about two thirds through the game. The game's save is kept between runs; the console's language is a setting. The second processor's music player is written natively.

Both screens in one window, any size, stacked, side by side or the touch screen alone, sharp pixels with smooth edges. Drawn through Vulkan, or the system's renderer where there is none. 3D scenes by the graphics hardware at up to 8 times the DS's resolution, battles too, with vertices between the DS's pixels so that models move smoothly, on one screen or both, or by the processor. Outlines (original thickness, 1 pixel or off), the smoothing of polygon edges, shadows and fog as on the DS. Widescreen: not yet.
Music and sound effects play through your audio device (SDL 3), kept in step with the frames. Settings, Sound: on or off, and the volume.
Keyboard, any number of controllers, the mouse as the stylus. Keys and buttons can be bound in Settings, Controls.

The launcher's first page is Play and your save, on the game's page of saves, and a gear to the settings; its other pages look like the game's settings menu; all from your ROM. The setup before the first build is in the program's own look. Settings book, pause menu. Report a problem opens a filled-in bug form on GitHub.
Window, files, settings, frame timing, log, checksums. A crash is noted with where it happened; a game that stops finishing frames too.

Every change is built and tested on Linux and Windows; green changes on main become a pre-release. Its description gives the state first, then the big changes since the last one. Issue forms for bugs, a stuck game or wrong graphics, and wishes.

next: First cave: not reached yet. The save starts in Saha Town, and scripted walks meet random battles. In Saha Town, black polygons that the game sends (vertex colour 0) cover the party with both 3D paths: the cause is still open.

Higher resolutions, 1: outlines and smoothed polygon edges on the graphics hardware follow the processor's rules, pixel for pixel in test scenes at 1x; still to be checked in the game (the cave) against the processor at 1x, and by eye at 4x.
Higher resolutions, 2: the 2D layers, sprites and text stay at the DS's resolution over the sharper 3D.
Higher resolutions, 3: a display capture that the game uses as a texture or as a scrolled background is read at the DS's resolution.
Higher resolutions, 4: the scroll of the 3D layer (BG0) is not used, by either 3D path.
Speed: the game's interrupt handler (0x01FFA900) still runs in the interpreter; it is reached only through a pointer set at run time.
